mainText:
Good morning, it's Saturday, Nov. 21.

Stock markets experience their worst week in over a year amid AI sell-off.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite closed down 5.3%, erasing all its gains for the year, amid mounting doubts about the AI industry. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both entered correction territory, meaning they've fallen more than 10% from recent peaks. The S&P 500 closed down 3.7% yesterday, while the Dow dropped 1.9%. Friday's declines were led by Anthropic, whose shares tumbled 8.5% after a successful IPO Thursday.
EU and UK strike post-Brexit deal on trade and youth mobility.
Officials announced the deal during a summit in Brussels yesterday, over a decade after the UK voted to leave the EU. The two sides agreed to link their
emissions trading systems
and align more closely on food safety and animal health rules, eliminating the need for most border checks on food. Up to 100,000 people under age 30 from each side can also reside in the other territory for up to three years without standard visa requirements.
White House names new cybersecurity director following series of outages.
Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies will replace Sean Cairncross as acting national cyber director. Cairncross, a lawyer with a background in Republican politics, was pushed out Thursday after a week of technology outages across the public and private sectors, including a multiday disruption to a classified National Security Agency network. Davies spent nearly two decades working on cyber risks in the private sector before joining the Pentagon last year.
Separately, a new federal report warns that the nation's food sector is
increasingly vulnerable
to cyberattacks; emergency response exercises haven't been conducted since 2024.
Texas execution takes over an hour as staff struggle to find vein.
Reinaldo Dennes was executed by lethal injection Thursday night for the 1996 murder of a diamond broker. Prison staff struggled to find a suitable vein, and Dennes was heard shouting in pain (
read
journalist's first-hand account, warning—sensitive). The execution comes amid renewed scrutiny of capital punishment following the failed execution of Christa Pike in September. A Texas spokesperson maintains that proper protocols were followed Thursday night.
European-Japanese spacecraft reach Mercury after 8-year journey.
The twin orbiters, jointly known as BepiColombo, are expected to enter Mercury's orbit today, becoming the second-ever mission to do so. The planet remains relatively unexplored, due in part to the sun's powerful gravitational pull; the journey took BepiColombo eight years. This mission aims to investigate Mercury's mysteriously icy craters and unusual surface hollows.
Federal prosecutors charge 14 in multimillion-dollar train heist.
The Department of Justice has charged 14 people in connection with an alleged Southern California cargo theft ring that stole more than $22.5M in merchandise, including Nike sneakers. The group allegedly targeted at least 36 trains over two years (
watch how
), coordinating via Instagram messages and selling the goods on the black market. The FBI estimates cargo theft losses in the US and Canada reached nearly $725M last year, a 60% increase from 2024.
Highly anticipated 'Hunger Games' prequel hits theaters this weekend.
Lionsgate's "Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is targeting a $100M domestic debut this weekend, though analysts project the film could earn upward of $130M. The adaptation of a Suzanne Collins novel, published last year, was produced on a roughly $150M budget and features original franchise star Jennifer Lawrence. The "Hunger Games" movies have grossed more than $3.3B worldwide, with "Catching Fire" leading the series at $865M.
